title: You didn’t stop praying.
paragraphs: And that’s the quiet kind of unbelief no one talks about.

You still show up.
Still serve.
Still say “God is good.”
But deep inside… something went silent.
Because how long do you wait before hope starts feeling foolish?
How many delayed answers before faith starts sounding like denial?

Not the loud rebellion.
Not the obvious sin.
The kind where your lips still pray—but your heart no longer leans forward.
“Both of them were righteous in the sight of God, observing all the Lord’s commands and decrees blamelessly.” — Luke 1:6
That’s where many believers quietly break.
But what happens when you obey… and heaven feels silent?
What happens when you do everything right…

“Maybe I don’t have enough faith.”
“Maybe God is disappointed in me.”
“Maybe this is just my life.”
You lower your expectations just enough to survive the disappointment.

You keep praying—but without fire.
You keep believing—but without anticipation.
And you don’t know how to receive it anymore.
When the angel appeared and said Elizabeth would have a son, his first response wasn’t worship.
“How can I be sure of this? I am an old man and my wife is well along in years.” — Luke 1:18

A man who knew the stories.
Abraham.
Sarah.
Miracles.
Delay had discipled his expectations more than Scripture did.
Delay can quietly reshape your theology if you’re not careful.
It can make you believe God used to move—but not anymore.
It can make you serve without expectancy.
“For you did not believe my words, which will come true at their appointed time.” — Luke 1:20
But because unbelief distorts who He is.
It turns a faithful God into a forgetful one.
A promise-keeper into a distant observer.
God did not cancel the promise.
The plan of redemption moved forward.
Do you see the grace in that?
Your moment of doubt does not erase God’s faithfulness.
Your wavering does not cancel His word.
Because your salvation—and your story—are not built on the perfection of your faith…
Because the story of Zechariah is not ultimately about a baby.
John the Baptist would prepare the way for Him.
The One who would not just answer prayers—
But deal with the deeper problem beneath them.
Sometimes what we call “waiting on God”…
is actually God exposing something in us.

Our need for control.
Our pride.
Our conditional trust.
“I trust You—as long as You move on my timeline.”
And Jesus didn’t come to negotiate.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
Every one of us has moments where we trust God with our lips…
but question Him in our hearts.
And that’s why we need the Gospel.
Jesus Christ stepped into our broken timeline.
Lived the perfect life we couldn’t live.
And rose again—proving that no delay, no doubt, no darkness has the final word.
“In him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, in accordance with the riches of God’s grace.” — Ephesians 1:7
Not based on how consistent your faith has been.
But based on His finished work.
So what do you do with your waiting?
What do you do with the prayers that feel unanswered?
You bring them back to Jesus.
Because God is not looking for perfect people.
Your greatest need is not the answer to your prayer.
Because even if every prayer gets answered…
without Christ, the soul is still empty.
Let Him rebuild the places where disappointment weakened your faith.
Let Him restore what delay tried to steal.
Not because of your track record…
“For no word from God will ever fail.” — Luke 1:37
That includes the word over your life.
Will you keep pretending everything is fine…
Or will you finally bring your real heart to God?
And if this stirred something in you…
